passage: Lichens are partnerships between a fungus and an alga, and for over a century they were described as involving just those two organisms. In 2016, researchers analyzing the genes active in common lichens found a third partner, a yeast, embedded in the outer layer of many species. The yeast had gone unnoticed partly because it is microscopic and partly because, under a microscope, it looks almost identical to the fungus's own cells. These findings imply that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: earlier descriptions of lichens may have been limited by the methods available to study them.
the yeast was introduced into most common lichens only a few years before the 2016 study took place.
lichens that contain the yeast cannot survive without frequent rainfall.
fungi and algae are no longer considered partners in most lichen species.
steps: The yeast was missed because it is tiny and looks like fungal cells under a microscope.
It was found through gene analysis, a different method.
So older descriptions were limited by microscopy.
Nothing suggests the yeast is new, that rainfall matters, or that the fungus-alga partnership is gone.
key: Inferences must follow from the reasons the text gives, here why the yeast was overlooked.
